newsitem.title: UK: GEC reviews defence deals but "in no rush".
newsitem.headline: GEC reviews defence deals but "in no rush".

text.p: Britain's General Electric Co Plc said on Tuesday it was examining deals to strengthen the position of its defence arm GEC Marconi.
Marconi was in good shape and GEC would not be rushed into forging link-ups for it, managing director George Simpson said.

"There are two points to consider. First, (defence arm) Marconi is the heart of GEC and it has a record order book in its own right. (Second) It will develop real shareholder value so I'm not under desperate time pressure to act," Simpson told Reuters in an interview.
"We are looking at Siemens Plessey (Siemens AG 's defence arm which is up for sale) and talking to Finmeccanica SpA," he added.
Simpson said he would be happy to "do these things" first, but said: "I must keep my eye on the ball elsewhere."
Consolidation among European defence players has taken on a new urgency since the mega-mergers in the U.S. between Lockheed Martin Corp and Northrop Grumman Corp plus Boeing Co and McDonnel Douglas

Asked about the re-emergence of rumours about a merger between GEC and British Aerospace Plc, Simpson said "I am sensitised to the situation with BAe and talk to them regularly as well as to Thomson-CSF in France."
He said he was also monitoring opportunities in the U.S.
